title: Paranoia
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with paranoia, auditory hallucinations (hearing voices), disorganized speech/behavior, negative symptoms (flat affect, social withdrawal, avolition), and functional decline >6 months. Schizophrenia is a chronic psychiatric disorder — symptoms for ≥6 months with ≥1 month of active symptoms. Must rule out substance-induced psychosis, medical causes (CNS tumor, infection, autoimmune encephalitis, thyroid), and other psychiatric disorders (bipolar with psychosis, schizoaffective). Diagnosis is clinical — no diagnostic test. Collateral history crucial. Treatment: antipsychotics (second-generation: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, aripiprazole — fewer EPS than first-gen like haloperidol). Clozapine for treatment-resistant. Monitor for metabolic syndrome (weight, glucose, lipids). Long-acting injectables for non-adherence. Psychosocial interventions: CBT, family therapy, supported employment. Safety assessment for self-harm/aggression.
